name: Ravyn Lenae
label: Atlantic
lede: She paid $300 for her first studio session as a high school sophomore, signed to Atlantic at 16, and made people wait until 23 for the debut album.

eras.title: Three hundred dollars and a scene
eras.text: A Chicago High School for the Arts kid lands in Classick Studios with Monte Booker and Smino, and Atlantic signs her at 16. Everything starts with a free download.

years.h: A $300 studio session becomes her first single, "Greetings"
years.p: Ravyn Lenae was a sophomore at the Chicago High School for the Arts, where she studied classical music, when she paid for the session.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, she spent $300 on a studio session as a high school sophomore to produce "Greetings". She had started writing songs back at Roseland Christian School on Chicago's South Side, and her maternal grandfather, Richard Williams, was a doo-wop group member and longtime pastor there.

years.cap: Zero Fatigue: Ravyn Lenae, Monte Booker and Smino.
years.h: Moon Shoes: a free download from Classick Studios
years.p: Her debut EP came out in August 2015 as a free download, made around Chris "Classick" Innumerable's Chicago studio with [[Monte Booker|3a8d955f-fe39-4092-97e7-29f9ada69490]] and [[Smino|96800e05-9924-4321-859a-76e0d4750f2f]].
years.xp:
Classick Studios is where she met Smino in 2015, and it is where the Zero Fatigue collective formed, with Booker, Lenae and Smino at its core, per Wikipedia. She had already been featured on Booker's "Baby" that year.

Atlantic later reissued Moon Shoes (2016) through Three Twenty Three Music Group.

eras.title: Noname, SZA, then Steve Lacy
eras.text: Atlantic signs her, Chicago's rappers put her on their records, and then two big tours and a full EP from Steve Lacy of The Internet make her the new R&B voice people in the know quote.

years.h: Atlantic signs her at 16 and reissues Moon Shoes
years.p: She also turned up on Mick Jenkins' The Healing Component and on [[Noname|1395c84b-2e84-4f25-9962-f1c0d5aa31ed]]'s "Forever" the same year.
years.xp: W Magazine reports she signed with Atlantic at 16 and toured with Noname while still in high school. Wikipedia dates the signing and the Atlantic and Three Twenty Three reissue of Moon Shoes to 2016.

years.h: Opening for Noname, then for SZA on the Ctrl tour
years.p: Noname's Telefone tour ran January to March 2017, and [[SZA|272989c8-5535-492d-a25c-9f58803e027f]]'s Ctrl tour picked her up from August to December.
years.xp: Refinery29 says Noname took her on her first tour and that the SZA run, the same year, convinced her she could headline on her own. She graduated high school in May 2017.

years.p: Rolling Stone put her on its "10 New Artists You Need to Know" list that March, and she played SXSW.
years.xp: Rolling Stone said the EP "delves into more romantic concerns with the same quiet grace", as quoted on Wikipedia.

years.h: Crush: five songs, all produced by Steve Lacy
years.p: Lacy executive-produced the EP and wrote every track with her; he sings on "Computer Luv" and "4 Leaf Clover".
years.xp: Wikipedia lists five tracks and a 16:33 running time. Pitchfork called it suited to "Quiet Storm radio" with a "methodical late-night vibe". Gothamist put it on its 2018 year-end albums list, and she performed on MTV's Total Request Live.

eras.title: Four years, one debut album
eras.text: She starts the album in 2019, loses the plan to the pandemic, moves from Chicago to Los Angeles, and comes out the other side with a 16-track debut that Pitchfork ranks No. 32 of 2022.

years.h: She starts Hypnos and commutes between Chicago and LA
years.p: She began the album after touring her Crush run, meeting producers in both cities.
years.xp:
W Magazine reports that the pandemic interrupted the process in 2020 and pushed her to relocate to Los Angeles, and that she finished mastering three days before their May 2022 interview.

On the gap, she said: "It's not about making enough songs."

years.h: "Skin Tight" with Steve Lacy is the first single
years.p: It was the first of four singles, followed by "Light Me Up", "M.I.A." and the [[Kaytranada|e56aee57-d90e-40cf-a70d-beb70f6f3c69]]-produced "Xtasy".

years.h: Hypnos lands: Pitchfork 8.5, Best New Music, No. 32 of 2022
years.p: Pitchfork gave the debut 8.5 and called it "a mature reintroduction"; NPR Music ranked it No. 18 of 2022.
years.xp:
Produced by Luke Titus, Steve Lacy, Monte Booker, Kaytranada, Sango and IAmNobodi, per Wikipedia, with recording running 2018 to 2022. Clash and Loud and Quiet each gave it 8/10. Complex placed it No. 30 and The A.V. Club No. 22 on year-end lists.

An "Xtasy" remix with Doechii followed in September 2022.

years.p: It was one of the first concerts back in the NPR building, with a six-piece band led by keyboardist Harrison "Achee" Hawkins.
years.xp: NPR's page lists bassist Marcus Reddick, drummer Danielle "Dee" Thompson, guitarist Garrett Jones and backing vocalists Aja Grant and Phylilia Hill. On "Inside Out" she said self-love is "a lifelong journey".

eras.title: The slow song that took over
eras.text: A second album with DJ Dahi, a TikTok mashup with Solange that arrives six months late, and a Hot 100 top five.

years.p: Pitchfork gave it 7.8; Metacritic lists 83 from six reviews. Features: Ty Dolla $ign and [[Childish Gambino|7fb57fba-a6ef-44c2-abab-2fa3bdee607e]].
years.xp: It was recorded in 2023 across three North Hollywood and Burbank studios, with Dahi and 11 other producers including Steve Lacy, Terry Lewis and Rascal. The lead singles "Love Is Blind" and "Love Me Not" came out on May 3, 2024. She described the record as "a return to a place of self-trust".

years.src: Wikipedia: Love Me Not · Wikipedia: Ravyn Lenae
years.h: A TikTok mashup with Solange turns "Love Me Not" into a hit
years.p: A user posted it over Solange's "Losing You" six months after release; the song reached No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the mashup came from a TikTok user called thatsode, and the song was soundtracking over 320,000 clips by April 2025. It entered the Hot 100 at No. 81 and climbed to No. 5, and reached No. 2 in the UK and Australia.

Certifications cited include 2x Platinum in the UK and 5x Platinum in Canada.

years.h: Sabrina Carpenter's tour, Coachella and a headline run
years.p: She joined [[Sabrina Carpenter|1882fe91-cdd9-49c9-9956-8e06a3810bd4]]'s Short n' Sweet Tour, played Coachella in April, and headlined in the US, UK and Europe that fall.
years.xp: Billboard named her R&B Rookie of the Year among its R&B/Hip-Hop Power Players, and "Love Me Not" was nominated for Song of Summer at the MTV VMAs, per Wikipedia.

years.p: Wikipedia lists her next album, Blue Island, for August 7, 2026.
